# SignalX Zero (@sigx/zero)

> Unstyled, accessible component primitives for the SignalX (sigx) framework.
> Components render a stable machine-readable anatomy — data-scope, data-part,
> data-state attributes — and NO styling. A design system is a separate,
> generatable artifact: typed tokens + recipes compiled to plain CSS by
> @sigx/zero-kit.

## The attribute contract

- Every part: `data-scope="<component>"` + `data-part="<part>"` (kebab-case).
- `data-state`: ONE value from a closed per-part set (open|closed,
  checked|unchecked, active|inactive).
- Boolean flags are presence-only: `data-disabled=""`, never ="false".
  Vocabulary: disabled, highlighted, selected, invalid, required, readonly,
  placeholder, focus-visible, pressed, press-animating.
- Press feedback (parts declaring the `pressed` flag): the runtime sets
  `data-pressed` while the pointer/key is down, and `data-press-animating`
  from press-start until the part's CSS animation ends (one-shot effects
  like ripples play out even on a quick tap), and writes the press point as
  `--press-x`/`--press-y`/`--press-r` (px; r = farthest-corner radius).
  Keyboard presses get centered coordinates. Lifecycle: a press ends when
  the gesture ends — an uncaptured pointerleave cancels it, a captured
  pointer (touch's implicit capture) holds it until release, and a drag
  surface (slider) attaches no pointerleave at all: a window-level release
  listener ends the press wherever the pointer lets go.
  Publishing parts: button root; tabs tab; dialog/popover/drawer
  trigger+close;
  menu trigger+item; select trigger+item and combobox trigger+item (items
  are pointer-only — keyboard selection lives on the trigger/input via
  aria-activedescendant); collapsible/accordion trigger;
  switch/checkbox control and radio-group item-control (press anywhere in
  the label row lands on the control; Space via the hidden input);
  slider control (`data-pressed` only — a drag has no one-shot);
  pagination item and prev/next triggers; steps item.
- Variant axes pass through as data-color / data-size / data-variant
  (values: color = any DS-declared role — recommended vocabulary
  primary|secondary|accent|neutral|info|success|warning|error,
  size = xs|sm|md|lg|xl, variant = design-system-defined), on the scope's
  CARRIER part (root, else the first part). A part that declares `carries`
  in its anatomy (timeline's marker, steps' item: ['color']) re-carries
  that axis: it takes the prop and renders the attribute itself, and the
  nearest carrier wins.
- Layout attributes render under the data-l- prefix from a CLOSED
  vocabulary zero owns (gap, gap-x, gap-y, pad, pad-x, pad-y, align,
  justify, wrap, cols, span, track, grow, axis, space). A part declares
  which ones it may carry as `layout` in its anatomy, exactly as it
  declares `placements`. Spacing values are the --space-* ramp plus `none`
  (none|2xs|xs|sm|md|lg|xl|2xl), so a layout prop cannot spell a gap the
  design system has no token for. Per-breakpoint values put the breakpoint
  in PREFIX position — data-l-gap="sm" with data-l-md-gap="lg" — which is
  what keeps the multi-word attributes (data-l-gap-x) unambiguous.
  Unlike a variant axis, this vocabulary is the same in every design
  system: the skin chooses what --space-md IS, not what "md" means.
- The full machine-readable registry ships as `@sigx/zero/manifest.json`:
  every component, part, state (as a ready-made CSS selector), flag and
  token hint — and per component a `models` block: what its API binds
  (`name` absent = the `model` prop, else `model:<name>`), the `concept`,
  the value `type`, the derived `default`/`change` companions, the compound
  `member` when not Root, `multiple`, `formControl`.

## The token contract

- Colors are a naming GRAMMAR, not a fixed vocabulary: each design system
  declares its own roles, emitted as `--color-<role>` with optional
  `--color-<role>-content` (readable foreground, contrast-validated) and
  `--color-<role>-soft` (derived tint). Only the base surfaces are fixed:
  base-100/base-200/base-300/base-content. A DS that declares nothing gets
  the recommended roles: primary/secondary/accent/neutral/info/success/
  warning/error.
- Non-color tokens work the same way: a closed set of CATEGORIES, each fixing
  a `--prefix-` and a value grammar, with OPEN keys inside that the design
  system declares. Today: `--radius-*` (selector|field|box), `--size-*`
  (selector|field), `--text-*` (xs…3xl), `--space-*`
  (2xs…2xl), `--shadow-*` (xs…xl), `--font-*` (FAMILIES: sans|serif|mono|
  display), `--weight-*`, `--leading-*`, `--tracking-*`, `--duration-*`
  (instant|fast|normal|slow), `--ease-*` (linear|standard|emphasized),
  `--border`, `--disabled-opacity`.
  The `recommended` keys are the ones `@sigx/zero/css` ships fallbacks for —
  declare any others you need and they flow into your manifest. The full
  table is `tokens.categories` in manifest.json.
- Category values are declared ONCE for the design system in
  `tokens.system`, not repeated per theme. `tokens.systemDark` overrides them
  for dark-scheme themes, and a single theme can override via its own
  `system` block. Resolution: `system` → `systemDark` → `theme.system`.
- `--font-*` is FAMILIES, never sizes; sizes are `--text-*`. The ramp is
  either listed in `typography.sizes` or generated from
  `typography.scale: { base, ratio }`, with `sizes` winning per key.
  Weights and leading are unitless.
- Motion: recipes write
  `transition: background var(--duration-fast) var(--ease-standard)`, never a
  literal duration. Every declared `--duration-*` collapses to 0.01ms under
  `prefers-reduced-motion: reduce`, so referencing the token is what makes a
  recipe honor the preference — a hardcoded `0.2s` opts out. (0.01ms rather
  than 0ms so `transitionend` / `animationend` still fire.) Don't tokenise a
  LOOPING animation's duration; it would speed up rather than stop.
- ANY token can differ by color scheme, not only colors. Colors use
  `light-dark()`; everything else (category values, declared `custom` tokens,
  `extra`, component overrides) is emitted in a `prefers-color-scheme: dark`
  block whenever the default light and dark themes disagree. Give a value a
  light counterpart if you want it to differ under dark — there has to be
  something for an explicitly-selected light theme to restate.
- Themes are selected via `data-theme` on any ancestor; the default
  light/dark pair uses CSS `light-dark()` so system scheme needs no JS.
- Cascade layers: `@layer zero.tokens, zero.recipes;` — app CSS is unlayered
  and always wins.

## Components (state via one two-way `model` prop, sigx Define.Model)

Bind a signal property with a getter: `model={() => state.open}` (sigx tracks
the read to write back — two-way, no onChange needed). Or stay uncontrolled
with `defaultOpen` / `defaultValue` / `defaultChecked`. The getter must read a
signal property directly, not a transformed expression.

THE NAMING RULE (every model, no exceptions): a model concept N has exactly
`default<N>` (the uncontrolled seed) and `<n>Change` (the change event,
handler `on<N>Change`). A named model's concept is its name
(`model:expandedValues` → `defaultExpandedValues` + `expandedValuesChange`).
The anatomy declares each model and manifest.json carries it; a parity test
holds the sources to it.

THE BINDING LAW: a zero model IS a sigx `Model`, and the native control a
component renders binds to it with `model=` — sigx's platform processor owns
write-back, so the wrapper is a superset of the raw element, never a subset.
`modelModifiers` (`trim`/`number`/`lazy`/`debounce`) on Input.Root and
Textarea.Root reach the native input; Checkbox bound to a `string[]` is
sigx's array mode; a RadioGroup.Item is a real radio bound to the group's
model. Transforms apply once at the component boundary, timing on the
element.

58 components ship today. Every part each renders is listed below, in
anatomy order; the authoritative machine-readable list (parts × states × flags
× token hints) is `@sigx/zero/manifest.json` — generate design systems against
that, not this summary.

`hidden-input` is a real, styleable part: form controls render an actual
native input so they post pre-hydration. Design systems normally hide it
visually while keeping it focusable, rather than `display: none`.

VISUALLY HIDDEN (#54) is NOT a flag and not a state: a part whose anatomy
declares `visuallyHidden: true` (field/input/textarea `label`, dialog/drawer
`title`, switch/checkbox `label`) renders `data-visually-hidden` when the
consumer asks (`visuallyHidden` on the part; `hideLabel` on Switch.Root and
Checkbox.Root), and zero's css/base.css clips it in `@layer zero.structure`.
A design system writes nothing for it and cannot undo it. `VisuallyHidden`
(asChild; no scope, no anatomy) hides arbitrary content the same way.
AUTOSIZE (#88) is the same kind of presentation request: `data-autosize` on
a part whose anatomy declares `autosize: true` (textarea's `textarea`),
sized by base.css in `@layer zero.structure`.

THE FORM CONTRACT (#441): every posting control takes `name`, `form`,
`disabled`, `invalid`, `required` (and `readonly` where the platform has
it), each the prop OR its Field's. It posts only while it has a `name`; a
disabled control never posts; `form="id"` associates it from outside the
form; the form's `reset()` restores the component default into model and
DOM. Select and Combobox post through a real visually-hidden `<select>`
(`hidden-input`, element select) — `required` is a platform constraint and
the invalid focus lands on the trigger/input.

Every component has a `Root` COMPONENT — it takes the `model` and the
configuration props, and always wraps the others. For Dialog, Popover,
Tooltip and Menu the root renders no DOM element of its own (it only provides
context), so those four have no `root` PART and nothing to select with
`[data-part="root"]`. Below, the slash-separated names are the parts a
component renders; the root is called out separately where it carries props.

- Button: Root(asChild) — one part on a native <button>, no machine states.
  Carries all three variant axes (color/size/variant), which is what it is
  for: it is where a design system puts its fill styles. Publishes press
  feedback (data-pressed / data-press-animating / --press-*), as do all
  interactive parts — see the press-feedback bullet above.
- Tabs: Root(model=value)/List/Tab(value,asChild)/Panel(value). APG tabs,
  roving arrows, automatic|manual activation, orientation.
- Collapsible: Root(model=open)/Trigger/Panel on native <details>. The
  panel is labelled by the trigger (no role) and publishes
  --collapsible-panel-height/--collapsible-panel-width (measured px); a
  close flips data-state to closed at once and keeps <details open> until
  the panel's own animations finish, so recipes animate the panel's closed
  state from var(--collapsible-panel-height) to 0 (web-only property).
- Accordion: Root(model=string[])/Item/Trigger/Panel on native <details>;
  `multiple`, `collapsible`, `orientation` (vertical default; data-orientation
  on root and trigger), `loop`, `regions`. APG keyboard: arrows move focus
  between enabled triggers, Home/End; no roving tabindex. Panels are
  role=region labelled by their trigger (`regions={false}` drops the role).
  Same size properties and deferred close as Collapsible, named
  --accordion-panel-height/--accordion-panel-width.
- Dialog: Root(model=open, modal, dismissible, role — renders no element)
  then Trigger/Popup/Title/Description/Footer/Close/Cancel on native <dialog>
  + top layer (no Portal). The backdrop is a `backdrop` part that renders no
  element on the web — recipes style `parts.backdrop` and the compiler
  projects it onto [data-scope="dialog"][data-part="popup"]::backdrop (states
  narrow the popup: [data-state="open"]::backdrop).
  role="alertdialog" is the APG alert-dialog preset on the same anatomy: the
  popup announces as alertdialog, a backdrop click does NOT dismiss (Escape
  still does, under `dismissible`), and initial focus goes to the
  least-destructive action — mark it with Dialog.Cancel, which closes like
  Close and carries `autofocus` in alertdialog mode so `showModal()`'s
  focusing steps land on it.
- Popover: Root(model=open, placement, offset, positionStrategy — renders no
  element) then Trigger/Popup/Title/Close, on the popover attribute + anchor
  positioning.
- Tooltip: Root(model=open, defaultOpen, openDelay, closeDelay, placement — renders no
  element) then Trigger/Popup.
- Menu: Root(model=open, defaultOpen, closeOnSelect, placement — renders no element) then
  Trigger/Popup/Item(asChild)/CheckboxItem/RadioGroup/RadioItem/Group/
  GroupLabel/Separator; `select` event.
  Stateful items (APG menuitemcheckbox/menuitemradio): CheckboxItem(value,
  model=checked, closeOnSelect default FALSE — unlike plain items, toggling
  keeps the menu open) and RadioGroup(model=value — renders the same labelled
  `group` part Menu.Group does)/RadioItem(value, closeOnSelect default
  FALSE). Both carry data-state checked|unchecked + aria-checked, emit the
  root's `select` alongside their own model events, and auto-render an
  `item-indicator` part mirroring the checked state — zero leaves it empty,
  the design system draws the mark (recipes key on
  [data-state="checked"]). asChild renders only the consumer's element.
  Context menu: ContextTrigger(asChild) wraps any surface — right-click /
  Android long-press opens the SAME popup at the pointer via a virtual
  anchor (deferred past the gesture: an auto popover opened mid-gesture
  would be light-dismissed by its own pointerup, racily); Shift+F10 /
  ContextMenu key open anchored to the surface RECT (keyboard has no
  pointer). A second right-click outside the popup repositions; last
  opener (Trigger vs ContextTrigger) wins the anchor. No iOS long-press
  (no native contextmenu there) — pair -webkit-touch-callout: none with
  your own recognizer for now.
  Submenus: Sub(model=open, placement default right-start with RTL flip,
  openDelay/closeDelay hover intent — renders no element) then
  SubTrigger(asChild)/SubPopup, nested to any depth inside a Popup. Item/
  Group/Separator work unchanged inside a SubPopup and `select` bubbles to
  the root. sub-trigger carries data-state open|closed AND the highlighted
  flag — style [data-state="open"] to keep it active while focus is in the
  submenu; sub-popup is a distinct part so it can animate on its own axis.
  Keyboard: ArrowRight/Enter/Space open + focus first item, ArrowLeft closes
  back (mirrored under RTL); Escape closes one level (native popover);
  hover opens without moving focus. Safe triangle: once a submenu is open,
  a mouse leaving its sub-trigger toward it does not hand hover to sibling
  items it crosses while it stays inside the triangle from the exit point
  to the popup's near edge; each move inside restarts closeDelay, so a
  pointer that stops lets the submenu close and the item under it take
  hover. Touch gets no triangle. No prop — it is always on.
- Select: Root(model=value | value[], model:open, items, itemKey, itemLabel,
  itemValue, itemDisabled, itemGroup, multiple, virtual, estimateItemSize,
  name, form, required, placeholder)/Trigger/Value/Indicator/Popup/Group/
  GroupLabel/Item/ItemIndicator/Spacer/HiddenInput (+ the group-heading
  part, rendered only by a windowed grouped list). TYPED GENERIC ROOT: T
  infers from `items`; the model holds the ITEM unless `itemValue` says what
  it holds (a value model: `itemValue={(c) => c.code}` → string; a number
  works too) — null while nothing is selected, `T | null` / `V | null`;
  `multiple` makes it an array.
  itemKey is the string identity (DOM id, typeahead, the posted value —
  default: an object's value/id or the primitive), itemLabel the display
  text (default: label or the key). THE COLLECTION IS THE TRUTH: labels and
  groups resolve from data before anything mounts. With `items` and no slot
  children the Root renders Trigger(Value, Indicator) + Popup(Item per item,
  Group/GroupLabel per distinct group in first-appearance order) through the
  SAME anatomy; the `item` slot ({ item }) customises an option's content;
  slot children win entirely when both are given. Hand-written Select.Item
  children register into the same collection. Option groups are the
  optgroup equivalent: role=group named by its GroupLabel while one is
  rendered. Under `multiple` a selection toggles, the popup stays open,
  Value joins the labels, the popup is aria-multiselectable. The hidden
  <select> carries every item as an option in data mode (autofill), the
  selection alone with hand-written items, and is `multiple` under multiple.
  The generated trigger has no aria-label: name an items-driven Select
  through a Field.
  WINDOWING (#96, Select and Combobox alike): `virtual={virtualListbox}`
  on a data-mode root renders only the options near the popup's scroll
  position (through createVirtualList); `estimateItemSize` (px, default 36)
  until measured. `virtual` takes the strategy, not a boolean:
  `import { virtualListbox } from '@sigx/zero/virtual-listbox'` (also on the
  barrel) — its own entry, so the select/combobox entries never carry
  windowing (#119).
  The highlighted option is pinned — always rendered, so
  aria-activedescendant never dangles — and keyboard moves (arrows,
  Home/End, typeahead, and PageUp/PageDown only while windowed) scroll to
  it; opening scrolls to the selection. Options carry aria-setsize (visible
  count) and aria-posinset. The popup is the scroll viewport: aria-hidden
  `spacer` parts (inline block-size, nothing to paint) stand in for skipped
  rows; base.css bounds a windowed popup at min(20rem, 60vh) in
  zero.fallback, so a popup recipe's max-block-size wins. Options stack as
  margin-less blocks. itemGroup groups window too (#127): each heading is a
  `group-heading` part — an aria-hidden ROW of the window, beside the
  options (no `group` element is rendered windowed), measured like one;
  options name it through aria-describedby while it is rendered, and the
  highlighted option's heading is pinned with it. Hand-written items are
  never windowed (`virtual` is ignored) — pass `items` to window. Windowed,
  the hidden <select> carries the chosen options only. Grouped, the
  keyboard walks the RENDER order (a group's later members pulled up under
  its heading), windowed or not.
- Switch: Root(model=checked)/Control/Thumb/Label/HiddenInput, role=switch.
- Checkbox: Root(model=checked | string[])/Control/Indicator/Label/HiddenInput;
  supports `indeterminate`. A `string[]` model is sigx's array mode: boxes
  sharing it toggle their own `value`'s membership; `checkedChange` reports
  THIS box's boolean.
- RadioGroup: Root(model=value, items, itemKey, itemLabel, itemDisabled, slot
  item)/Label/Item/ItemControl/ItemIndicator/ItemLabel/HiddenInput;
  orientation. `items` renders one radio per item (explicit children win
  entirely); the model stays the STRING a native radio group posts, so
  itemKey IS the posted value (defaults: value / id / the primitive).
- Slider: Root(model=number|number[], min, max, step, largeStep,
  minStepsBetweenThumbs, name, invalid, marks, getValueText, onValueCommit)/Label/Control/Track/Range/Thumb/Mark/ValueText/HiddenInput.
  Two projections over one anatomy. Scalar model: render Slider.Control — a
  native <input type=range> bound with model= to the first value (a derived
  Model whose write quantizes and clamps), single thumb, platform
  keyboard/forms/a11y.
  Range model (number[]): compose the real parts — Slider.Track wrapping
  Slider.Range and one Slider.Thumb(label, index?) per value, in order.
  Each thumb is an APG role=slider tab stop: arrows step (RTL-aware),
  PageUp/PageDown and Shift+Arrow move by largeStep (default 10*step; the
  native control takes these large steps too), Home/End go to its ALLOWED
  bounds — thumbs cannot cross, so each clamps at its neighbor plus
  minStepsBetweenThumbs*step and announces the clamp as aria-valuemin/max;
  aria-valuetext comes from getValueText(value, index). Track presses move
  the nearest thumb and start a drag; range spans lowest→highest (min→value
  when single); `marks` renders positioned `mark` tick parts (with label
  text) inside the track; a range model posts one hidden input per value
  under the shared `name`. Zero positions structurally (absolute + logical
  inset-inline-start percents — RTL mirrors for free) and paints nothing:
  recipes center the thumb with a negative margin-inline-start of half its
  width and own every color. --slider-percent still tracks the (highest)
  value's fraction. valueCommit (an event, NOT a model — no <n>Change pair)
  fires with the model's shape once per drag end, per keyboard step and on
  the native control's change, each only when the value moved.
- Progress: Root/Label/Track/Range/ValueText; `value: number | null`
  (null = indeterminate). Root renders aria-valuetext and the default
  ValueText paints the SAME string (#274): getValueText(value, {min, max,
  percent}) if given, else Intl.NumberFormat(locale, formatOptions), formatOptions
  merged over {style:'percent'} (percent/100) (another style formats the value).
  Indeterminate: no valuetext. Pass `locale` under SSR.
- RadialProgress: Root/Label/ValueText — circular progress as its OWN scope
  (a radial has no track/range geometry: the ring is one painted layer on
  the root, so reusing progress's anatomy would ship dead parts, and a
  data-mod is a styling hook, not a structural switch). Shares linear
  progress's value model verbatim: value number|null (null=indeterminate),
  min/max, role=progressbar + aria value trio, states
  loading|complete|indeterminate, and the SAME runtime-published
  --progress-percent — recipes paint the arc from it via conic-gradient
  masks over a background-color ink, and stop the indeterminate loop under
  reduced motion. Value text (aria-valuetext + default ValueText) is
  Progress's: getValueText / locale / formatOptions, default a percent.
- Field: Root/Label/Description/Error — wires ids and disabled/invalid/
  required down to the control it wraps, and its `size` when the control
  sets none (#57): a sized Field is a sized control.
  Validation (#284): the control reports its native element; Root takes
  `validate(value, validity) => string | string[] | null` (pushed through
  setCustomValidity, so native submit blocks on it) and `validateOn`
  (submit|blur|change; after a failed submit every change revalidates).
  Error takes `match` (a ValidityState key | 'custom' | true) and, with no
  children, renders the current message. A Field rendering an Error cancels
  the `invalid` bubble and focuses the form's first invalid control.
- Input: Root(model=string, model:visible)/Label/Control/Input/Adornment/ClearTrigger/
  VisibilityTrigger, a single-line text field.
  `type` is text|email|password|search|tel|url only (number is NumberInput;
  the selection and date/time types are not text fields). The model writes
  through on every keystroke — no draft/commit split; `modelModifiers`
  (`lazy`, `debounce`, `trim`) defer or shape it exactly as on a bare
  <input>. `control` is the field chrome (border/ring/invalid tint), the
  <input> inside it is transparent. NO hidden input: the visible <input> IS
  the form control and carries `name`. AFFORDANCES live in the control:
  Adornment(placement: start|end → data-placement; consumer content, a
  press on non-interactive content focuses the input), ClearTrigger(label,
  default "Clear"; tabindex=-1, aria-controls the input, rendered only while
  the value is non-empty, disabled while disabled or readonly; empties the
  value like typing — model write, valueChange, an input event — and
  focuses the input) and VisibilityTrigger(label, default "Show password";
  states on|off, aria-pressed; toggles Root's model:visible /
  defaultVisible / visibleChange, and while visible a type=password input
  renders type=text; slot gets { visible }). In a type=search field Escape
  clears a non-empty value and is preventDefault-ed so dismiss layers
  yield; an empty field lets it through.
- Card: Root/Header/Title/Description/Body/Footer. No state, no context, no
  ids — a styling container. Title renders <h3> so a page of cards is
  navigable from a heading list. Every part below Root is optional.
- Alert: Root(model=open, default TRUE)/Icon/Title/Description/Close.
  role=alert on Root; a live region announces CHANGES, so a server-rendered
  alert is silent at load and one inserted later is announced. Close sets the
  model false and the runtime sets `hidden` (anatomy: hiddenIn: ['closed']),
  so design systems never paint `closed`. Icon is aria-hidden. Root is
  aria-labelledby Title / aria-describedby Description (presence-tracked);
  live="polite" renders role=status instead (#274). Closing while focus is
  inside moves it to finalFocus(), else the nearest focusable sibling
  before the root, else leaves it.
- EmptyState: Root/Icon/Title/Description/Actions (#131) — what stands where
  the content would be: nothing yet, nothing found, nothing reachable. No
  state and no behaviour (presence is the consumer's `if`); no role of its
  own (pass `role="status"` to have a failure announced); Title takes
  asChild so it can be the heading the page's outline wants; Icon is
  aria-hidden; Actions is a band for the consumer's own Button.Root (or a
  `Button.Root asChild` over an <a>). The tone is the `color` axis, Alert's
  answer: a failure is `error`, an offline notice `warning`. Not an Alert —
  an alert announces itself and can be dismissed; an empty state is the
  page's content while there is none.
- Badge: Root/Dot — the carrier IS the text-bearing part, which is why it is
  the one scope that can wire its own `variant` vocabulary against the
  contrast audit's one-element probe. asChild. Dot (#130) is an optional
  aria-hidden status dot: it re-carries `color` (carries: ['color'] — a dot
  with its own colour is the status while the pill's colour is its tone; a
  dot without one follows the pill, nearest carrier wins, and on an
  uncoloured pill it is the ink) and has one state, `running` (the governed lifecycle spelling,
  absent at rest — a pulse in every skin with a static halo under reduced
  motion). It is paint, in the indicator contrast matrix.
- Kbd: Root only, on a semantic <kbd> — the element is the meaning, so there
  is no asChild to swap it away. No states; size is the axis that matters.
- Status: Root only — an empty presence dot the design system paints. NO
  states on purpose: online/busy/degraded are colours of one resting render
  (the `color` axis), not a machine lifecycle. Without `label` it is
  aria-hidden (the visible text beside it carries the meaning); with `label`
  it announces as role="img" — not role="status", which is a live region.
- Indicator: Root/Item(placement) — anchors the item to a corner/edge of
  whatever Root wraps (badge on a button, dot on an avatar). Item stamps
  data-placement from a declared eight-slot subset: top-start|top|top-end|
  start|end|bottom-start|bottom|bottom-end — all LOGICAL (start/end are the
  reading-direction inline sides, added to the placement vocabulary for it;
  no left/right), so recipes position with inset-inline-* and RTL mirrors
  free. No ARIA of its own: meaning belongs to the item's content.
- Stats: Root(orientation)/Item/Title/Value/Desc/Figure — Card's cousin: a
  styling container for figures with labels, no state, no ids, no ARIA.
  BOTH root and item carry data-orientation (the between-item divider is
  directional CSS on the item, and a sibling selector cannot see the root —
  the toggle-group precedent). Every band below Item is optional. Item
  RE-CARRIES the colour axis (anatomy `carries: ['color']`, #161):
  Item(color) renders data-color on the item and outranks the root's, so
  one figure paints its own tone and its bands follow; an item without one
  follows the root. The bands (Title/Value/Desc/Figure) take no colour.
  Key the colour values on `item` in the recipe.
- Timeline: Root(orientation, default VERTICAL — a feed grows downward)/
  Item/Marker/Connector/Content(placement start|end). A real <ul>/<li> list
  so AT announces and walks it. Marker (the dot/icon on the axis — a paint
  part, graded by the contrast audit's indicator matrix) and Connector (the
  line toward the next item) are aria-hidden decoration; Content declares
  which SIDE of the axis it sits on as data-placement from the logical
  start|end pair, so alternating layouts are per-item markup and RTL
  mirrors free. Content and connector also carry data-orientation — a
  recipe composes side × axis on the element that has both. A timeline
  with no start-placed content should reserve no start track: the shipped
  skins collapse it with a `:has()` rule on the root (#57), no prop.
  Marker RE-CARRIES the colour axis (anatomy `carries: ['color']`, #94):
  Marker(color) renders data-color on the marker and outranks the root's,
  so each entry paints its own tone; a marker without one follows the
  root. Key the colour values on `marker` in the recipe.
- Chat: Root(placement start|end, default START — the reading edge is the
  other party in every messenger; your own rows opt into end)/Avatar/Header/
  Bubble/Footer. One message row, pure content: no state, no ids, no ARIA —
  a transcript needing log semantics is a role="log" container the consumer
  writes around the rows. Avatar is a SLOT (zero's Avatar, an <img>,
  initials). The colour axis rides the row and recipes wire it to the
  BUBBLE's fill; placement is logical, so RTL mirrors free.
- Join: Root(orientation)/Item(asChild) — visual grouping that collapses
  the radii of adjacent children (segmented search field, button strip).
  Pure CSS composition: two attribute carriers, no state, no ARIA (a join
  is a visual group; a consumer who means toolbar/group writes the role).
  Both root and item carry data-orientation (the collapse is item + item
  directional CSS). asChild is the honest joint: a wrapper cannot collapse
  the radius of the control inside it, so put the item attributes ON the
  control.
- Stack: Root(orientation, gap/gapX/gapY, pad/padX/padY, align, justify,
  wrap)/Item(asChild, grow) — the flex row or column an application layout
  is made of. Row and Col are the SAME scope with a different default
  orientation, exported as presets: two scopes would mean two recipes and
  two chances for a skin to paint them differently. Prefer them over
  `<Stack orientation=…>`; Stack itself defaults to horizontal, matching
  data-orientation everywhere else in zero rather than the vertical default
  some other libraries give this name. Spacing props take a rung of the
  --space-* ramp (or a breakpoint record), never a length. Item exists only
  so a child can opt into growing, and supports asChild for Join's reason:
  flex-grow applies to the flex ITEM, so a wrapper cannot grow the control
  inside it. No role — a stack is visual grouping.
- Container: Root only(measure, pad/padX/padY) — bounds the page width and
  keeps content off the edges. `measure` is xs|sm|md|lg|xl|prose|full from
  the design system's own --measure-* ramp, a token category of its own
  because the density ramp cannot reach page scale (--space-* tops out around
  1.5rem). Deliberately NOT the `size` axis: size="lg" on a Button means a
  chunkier button and on a Container would mean a wider page, and those ramps
  have no reason to move together; `prose` (a reading measure in ch) is not a
  size at all. `full` is `none`, not 100% — a container told not to bound
  itself should have no maximum. Unbounded by default. No colour: a container
  is a constraint, not a surface — wrap it around a Box.
- Box: Root only(color, pad/padX/padY) — the layout tier's one scope that
  PAINTS: a padded surface tinted by meaning. Card is the structured sibling
  (header/body/footer); Box is the unstructured one — a callout, a well, a
  panel. Follows Card's axis answer rather than inventing a second: color
  wired, variant NOT (no surveyed system varies a plain surface's chrome; the
  ones that do call it a Card). SIZE is declared out of existence, which is
  the one departure from Card: a Box's size IS its padding and `pad` already
  says that. The tint is the role's `-soft` derivation and the ink is the
  role itself — a large area of `--color-error` is a warning label, not a
  container. display:flow-root, so a child's margin cannot collapse out
  through the padding.
- Grid: Root(cols, track, gap/gapX/gapY, pad/padX/padY, align, justify)/
  Cell(asChild, span) — two-dimensional layout where Stack is
  one-dimensional. cols is a twelve-column count or `auto`; `auto` is
  repeat(auto-fit, minmax(min(100%, track), 1fr)), which reflows by available
  width with NO breakpoint named, and is what a collection of cards wants.
  track sets how narrow a column may get first. Counts compile to
  minmax(0, 1fr), not a bare 1fr: a track's implicit minimum is `auto`, which
  refuses to shrink below its content and is the usual reason a grid
  overflows. Cell exists because grid-column is a property of the grid ITEM,
  so a wrapper cannot make the child span; span="full" is 1 / -1. No role — a
  CSS grid is visual arrangement, and zero ships a Table for the other thing.
- Center: Root only(axis, pad/padX/padY, gap) — place-items on a
  single-child grid, the one construction that centres on both axes without
  caring what the child is. axis is both|inline|block, LOGICAL; the one-axis
  values pin the other to stretch, so axis="inline" does not also collapse
  the child vertically. Distinct from <Row justify="center" align="center">,
  which centres a row's CONTENT along its own axes.
- Spacer: Root only(space) — flexible room by default, a fixed rung of the
  spacing ramp when given `space`. aria-hidden: it holds room, never
  content. Earns its place next to `gap` because the two answer different
  questions: gap spaces EVERY child equally, a spacer pushes ONE boundary
  apart (the toolbar whose actions sit at the far end), which otherwise
  needs the row split into nested stacks.
- Carousel: Root(label REQUIRED — the root is a region, and a nameless
  region is an axe violation)/Viewport/Item/PrevTrigger/NextTrigger/
  IndicatorGroup/Indicator(index). A scroll-snap viewport whose MODEL IS
  THE ACTIVE INDEX: derived from real scroll by an IntersectionObserver
  (created only in onMounted — SSR never observes) and driven back on model
  set by scrolling the VIEWPORT alone (viewport.scrollTo, never
  scrollIntoView — the page never moves, #171; RTL-correct), smooth unless
  prefers-reduced-motion asks for a jump. APG carousel ARIA: region + aria-roledescription=carousel;
  items are "slide" groups labelled "n of m". Prev/next CLAMP (no wrap)
  and disable at their bounds; the dots are labelled BUTTONS (not tabs, no
  roving tabindex), the active one carrying aria-current. item and
  indicator ride data-state active|inactive; the indicator is a paint part
  graded by the contrast audit's indicator matrix. Horizontal only.
- Diff: Root(model=percent 0-100, default 50, disabled)/Before/After/
  Handle(label, getValueText, step=1, largeStep=10) — a
  before/after reveal whose divider HANDLE IS AN APG SLIDER: role=slider,
  aria-valuenow 0-100, aria-valuetext getValueText(v) (default "50%"),
  arrows ±step, PageUp/PageDown and Shift+Arrow ±largeStep, Home/End
  (RTL-aware — ArrowRight increases in LTR, decreases in RTL, so the handle
  always moves the way the key points), pointer drag with window listeners that survive
  leaving the box. The panes are CONTENT and stay inert. The runtime
  publishes --diff-percent on the root and positions the handle at the
  logical inset-inline-start; recipes clip the after pane with a LOGICAL
  inline-size (never a physical clip-path), so RTL mirrors free — the
  physical result is measured in e2e/diff.spec.ts. Size pane content to
  the ROOT, not the pane: the after pane clips by width. The handle is a
  paint part graded by the contrast audit's indicator matrix. Root disabled
  → data-disabled on root and handle, aria-disabled, no tab stop, no keys,
  no drag; recipes treat the handle, never the content panes.
- FileUpload: Root(model=File[], defaultFiles, maxFiles, minFileSize, maxFileSize,
  validate, directory, capture, onFilesReject)/Label/Trigger/ClearTrigger/Input/
  Dropzone/ItemGroup/Item(file, invalid)/ItemName/ItemSize/ItemRemove. The INPUT IS THE CONTROL — a
  real <input type=file> holding name/accept/multiple/required and posting
  its FileList natively — visually hidden and out of the tab order; the
  TRIGGER (a real <button>) is the one keyboard path to the picker. The
  DROPZONE is a pointer affordance only: never focusable, no role (APG has
  no drop-target pattern; a click forwards to the picker). Drag-over is
  the shared data-highlighted FLAG (stamped on dropzone AND root), not a
  new state. multiple appends across selections (dedupe name+size+
  lastModified); single replaces; drops are filtered by accept so the two
  ingestion paths agree; the input's own FileList is re-synced through
  DataTransfer best-effort. Field-context aware exactly like Input (the
  trigger owns the field's control id). ItemName/ItemSize default to the
  file's name and human-readable size; ItemRemove is labelled
  "Remove <name>" and hands focus to the next file's remove button (else
  the previous one, else the trigger). CONSTRAINTS run over both paths:
  each candidate is checked for accept ('invalid-type'), maxFileSize
  ('too-large'), minFileSize ('too-small') and the app's validate (any
  string codes); otherwise-valid files past maxFiles (or past the one slot
  in single mode) get 'too-many'. Accepted files join the model; the rest
  are reported through the filesReject EVENT as { file, errors }[] — never
  a model — and the input's FileList is re-synced so a refused file never
  posts. Render a refused file through Item invalid for data-invalid.
  ClearTrigger (default aria-label "Clear files") empties the model, renders
  nothing while it is empty, and focuses the trigger. A required upload
  left empty cancels the platform's bubble (it would anchor to the 1px
  input), focuses the trigger and reads invalid until the files change.
- Countdown: Root(label -> role=timer)/Value(value, digits)/digits —
  display-only numbers; the APP OWNS TIME. No internal timer, deliberately:
  a timer is app logic (which clock, paused when, what at zero) and an SSR
  hazard, so the component only renders the `value` it is given. Root
  composes units (hours/minutes/seconds are separate Values, separators
  are consumer text); each value publishes --countdown-value and renders
  real digit text (AT reads "10:04" off the DOM), zero-padded to `digits`
  and clamped at 0. The digits element is KEYED by its text, so each tick
  replaces it and a recipe's enter animation (translate/fade) plays once —
  collapsed to a cut under reduced motion. No states, no flags. The
  shipped skins declare an `inline` modifier (`mods={{ inline: true }}`)
  for one line inside a sentence: the text's own size and weight instead
  of the display step (#57).
- Swap: Root(model=boolean — concept `active`: defaultActive + activeChange,
  daisy's own word; the faces keep data-state on|off)/On/Off — two faces
  over one boolean. BOTH
  faces stay rendered (the component exists for the CSS transition between
  them; `hidden` computes display:none and would kill it) and the inactive
  one is aria-hidden. All three parts ride data-state on|off. DISPLAY by
  default (a span, no semantics — a theme icon following external state);
  `interactive` renders a real <button> that toggles on click (platform
  Enter/Space): with `label` (or aria-label/labelledby) aria-pressed carries
  the state and both faces are aria-hidden; unlabelled, the active face is
  the name, no aria-pressed, and it console-warns (#274). No indeterminate face —
  the model is a boolean, and rotate/flip looks are recipe styling, not
  contract.
- Table: Root/Table/Caption/Head/Body/Foot/Row/HeaderCell/Cell — semantic
  data table over the REAL table elements (caption/thead/tbody/tfoot/tr/th/
  td; the elements are the semantics, so no asChild anywhere). Root is the
  SCROLL CONTAINER — a <table> cannot be its own overflow box, so the
  wrapper div is anatomy, carries the axes, and recipes give it
  overflow-x auto. No states; a row can carry the shared data-selected
  flag (`selected` prop). Zebra striping and hover-highlight are design-
  system mods (data-mod-* on the root) in the skins that offer them, never
  anatomy. Sorting is deliberately out: header-cell renders the <th> that
  will carry aria-sort later. Write a Caption — it is the table's
  accessible name.
- Divider: Root only, role=separator, orientation. Non-focusable;
  aria-orientation emitted only for `vertical`.
- Navbar: Root/Start/Center/End — the landmark header bar, pure
  composition (no states, no behavior). Root is a <header> (the banner
  landmark at document scope), NOT a <nav>: the bar holds non-navigation
  content too, so the consumer wraps the actual link set in its own
  labelled <nav> inside a section. start/end are the logical pair, so RTL
  mirrors free.
- NavList: Root(label)/Group/Heading/List/Item/Link(current,asChild)/Icon/
  Meta (#132) — the sidebar's navigation list, and the <nav> Navbar points
  at: exactly the links. Root is a labelled <nav> landmark over <ul> lists;
  Link is an <a> whose `current` renders aria-current="page" +
  data-state="active" (Breadcrumbs' rule: the current page is the
  activation STATE, never a flag; the others are `inactive`). Group is a
  role="group" named by its Heading (ids wired for you); Icon is
  aria-hidden; Meta is the trailing slot (a Badge count, a Kbd hint) skins
  push to the far edge. No behaviour: the router passes `current` in.
  Renders inside a responsive Drawer.Panel as it renders anywhere.
- Breadcrumbs: Root(label)/List/Item/Link(current,asChild)/Separator — the
  APG breadcrumb pattern: <nav aria-label="Breadcrumb"> around an <ol>
  (order IS the meaning). The current page's link carries
  aria-current="page" and data-state="active" (the activation pair —
  data-current is not in the flag vocabulary and the synonym table rules
  current → active); every other link is "inactive". The separator is
  aria-hidden punctuation inside the item (default glyph /, replaceable
  slot) so the <ol> keeps only <li> children.
- Drawer: Root(model=open, modal: boolean | { below: bp }, dismissible,
  placement start|end, label — renders no element) then Trigger/Panel/Title/Close on native <dialog>
  + top layer, Dialog's machinery inherited (backdrop = ::backdrop pseudo
  part; presence-tracked aria-labelledby, with the label prop as the
  aria-label fallback when no Title renders — a nav drawer often has no
  visible heading). The panel stamps data-placement="start|end" from the
  LOGICAL pair (an edge panel anchors to the reading direction); recipes
  pin it with inset-inline-* so RTL mirrors free, and distinguish modal
  from inline with data-l-dock="sheet|inline" on the panel (#83) — the
  regime, not the open state, so unlike :modal it holds through a sheet's
  exit and the sheet keeps its box while it leaves. material, daisyui,
  heroui and carbon slide the sheet (translate over --drawer-travel, flipped
  by placement and :dir(rtl), dropped under reduced motion); basic and
  brutalist fade. modal (default)
  = showModal(): focus trap, Escape via cancel, scrim click dismisses by
  Dialog's click geometry. modal={false} = INLINE: renders in flow via
  show(), no dismiss trap (outside clicks are a non-event), Escape still
  closes through the dismissable behavior, focus restore covered by zero
  since show() provides neither. Panel(measure) sizes the panel from the
  --measure-* ramp (layout attribute data-l-measure, NOT the size axis —
  size rides the trigger, which the panel is not inside): recipes read
  --l-measure as a max-inline-size over inline-size: 100% (border-box) —
  the panel fills its container inline, or the viewport as a modal sheet,
  up to the measure; the table spells `full` as `none`, valid only for a
  max, so `full` is a full-screen sheet. Each recipe declares its own
  default --l-measure on the panel. modal={{ below: 'md' }} = RESPONSIVE
  (#82): a modal sheet below the design system's md, docked open inline at
  or above it. The model governs the sheet only (docked ignores it; Close,
  Escape and writes do nothing visible); crossing the breakpoint reports
  nothing (no openChange, no close) and a sheet open when the viewport
  widens is reset silently. SSR renders docked (panel open in markup;
  trigger, panel and close stamped data-l-dock-above="md" — a
  breakpoint-valued layout attribute like Table's stack, declared
  layout: ['dock-above'] on those parts), and the
  kit's per-breakpoint rules in @layer zero.structure hide trigger + close
  at/above md and the docked panel below md unless :modal. Focus: an
  outgrown sheet keeps focus in place; focus in a docked panel that stops
  showing moves to the trigger. A closed panel is display:none structurally (base.css), like
  Dialog's popup.
- Steps: Root(model=step value, defaultStep, loop, label, orientation)/
  Item(value,color,asChild)/Indicator/Separator/Title/Description — the wizard
  step rail, promoted from the ecosystem ext-stepper pattern (the
  zero-ext-example package REMAINS as the ecosystem acceptance test).
  role="group" + aria-label; arrow keys rove focus without changing the
  step (orientation-aware), click/Space/Enter select, ONE tab stop on the
  active step, aria-current="step". States are the active|complete|
  inactive family: complete is position-derived (before the current step,
  DOM order). The indicator mirrors its item's phase; the separator — the
  line from its item toward the next, aria-hidden, inside the item like
  timeline's connector — carries only complete|inactive (complete once
  its OWN item is complete; an active item's separator is inactive: the
  walk has reached it, not crossed it). Title/description carry no
  states; style them through the item's state. Item RE-CARRIES the colour
  axis (anatomy `carries: ['color']`, #112): Item(color) renders data-color
  on the item and outranks the root's, so one step paints its own tone
  (daisy's step-error) and everything inside it follows; an item without
  one follows the root. Key the colour values on `item` in the recipe.
- Pagination: Root(model=page, count, siblingCount, boundaryCount, label,
  prevLabel/nextLabel, pageLabel(n) — default "Page n") — options-driven: the row derives from count + the
  model, so zero renders item buttons, aria-hidden ellipses and the
  prev/next triggers itself. Constant-width windowing (the sibling block
  slides near the edges instead of shrinking); rows are keyed by page, so a
  sliding window keeps focus on the activated page. The current item carries
  aria-current="page" + data-state="active". Ordinary buttons in the nav
  landmark — deliberately no roving tabindex (no APG pagination pattern;
  each page is its own meaningful tab stop). The triggers carry the ‹/›
  glyph (Select.Indicator's convention), named by aria-label; recipes flip
  the glyph under RTL (scaleX(-1) under the skin's rtl guard).
- Skeleton: Root only(model=loading, default TRUE), data-state loading|loaded,
  aria-busy and inert while loading. Children stay in the DOM in BOTH states — the
  component exists to hold the layout its content will occupy, so the recipe
  paints OVER them while loading. No hiddenIn: the states differ by paint, so
  every design system must tell them apart.
- Spinner: Root only, no state — it spins or it is not rendered.
  role=status whose words are TEXT in a visually hidden `label` part
  (label ?? aria-label ?? "Loading"; no aria-label on the root — #274);
  `decorative` drops role and label and sets aria-hidden. The mark is
  the design system's, drawn on the root. Both loop, so both owe a prefers-reduced-motion answer
  that STOPS rather than collapsing the duration to ~0 (which strobes).
- Textarea: Root(model=string)/Label/Textarea. Input's shape minus `control`
  — nothing sits inside a textarea for a wrapper to hold, so the chrome draws
  on the element. `rows` passes through and `resize` is the design system's
  call — unless Root sets `minRows`/`maxRows` (#88): then the box AUTOSIZES
  (soft wraps included) between those line counts and scrolls past the max.
  The textarea part renders `data-autosize` + `--textarea-min-rows`/
  `--textarea-max-rows`; css/base.css grows it (`field-sizing: content`, `lh`
  bounds, `resize: none`) in `@layer zero.structure`, so a design system
  writes nothing. `createAutosize` measures the border-box chrome
  (`--textarea-block-chrome`) and is the scrollHeight fallback where
  `field-sizing` is unsupported. No hidden input, same reason as Input's.
  `modelModifiers` reach the textarea as on Input.
- Avatar: Root/Image(src, alt, asChild)/Fallback. Display-only; every part
  mirrors the load status as data-state="loading|loaded|error" (no src →
  error). Zero toggles `hidden` (fallback while loaded, image while error), so
  recipes must not set `display` on those parts unconditionally — style
  `&:not([hidden])` instead. Server markup always renders `loading`; the
  status resolves on mount; with no Image rendered it settles to error
  (#274). Fallback `delay` ms keeps it out of the DOM until the delay passes
  (client timer; SSR renders none). `statusChange` event.
- Toast: Viewport(placement, toaster, label, hotkey)/Root(toast)/Title/
  Description/Action/Close, over an imperative queue:
  `toast({ title, color, duration, role })` (browser-only), `createToaster()`
  for apps/tests, `useToaster` injectable. Viewport is a popover="manual" top
  layer, `role=region`, and the one polite live region (`aria-live=polite`);
  `role: 'alert'` toasts speak through a sibling visually-hidden assertive
  span instead (their root is `aria-live=off`). Each root is a focusable
  (`tabindex=-1`) named `role=group`, carries `data-color` +
  `data-placement`, and publishes `--toast-index`/`--toast-count`. F8
  (`hotkey`, `false` to disable; the label template's `{hotkey}` names it)
  focuses the first toast, Escape dismisses the focused one, and closing a
  focused toast hands focus to the next/previous toast or back to where it
  came from. Timers pause on hover, focus, a hidden tab or a blurred
  window; a toast arriving while shown re-stacks the viewport to the top of
  the top layer (inert under a modal dialog, by spec). PRESENCE IS RUNTIME-MANAGED —
  the one exception to the declarative presence rule: roots mount `closed`,
  flip `open` a frame later, and stay mounted after dismissal until their
  longest transition/animation ends. Style the plain two-state transition;
  never `@starting-style`/`allow-discrete` on toast parts, and gate any
  viewport `display` behind `&:popover-open`.
- Combobox: Root(model=value | value[], model:inputValue, model:open, items,
  itemKey, itemLabel, itemValue, itemDisabled, itemGroup, filter, emptyText,
  multiple, allowCustom, virtual, estimateItemSize, name, form, required,
  readonly, placeholder; `tag` slot)/Control/Tags/Tag(value)/TagLabel/
  TagRemove(label)/Input/Trigger/Popup/Group/GroupLabel/Item(asChild)/
  ItemIndicator/Spacer/Empty/HiddenInput. The same typed generic root and
  collection as Select, and the same `virtual` windowing (see Select); a new
  query scrolls back to the highlight, or the top. APG
  editable combobox: focus stays in the real <input> (role=combobox,
  aria-autocomplete=list, aria-activedescendant); Control is the field
  chrome wrapping input + trigger and mirrors open/invalid/focus-visible so
  the ring draws on the box. FILTERING: with `items`, zero filters — the
  default is a case-insensitive contains-match on the label as you type,
  `filter={(item, query) => …}` replaces it, `filter={false}` shows every
  item (a server-filtered list: pass what came back). Hand-written
  Combobox.Item children stay consumer-filtered — what you render is what
  is visible. Empty renders its content only while the visible list is
  empty (the data expansion renders it from `emptyText`). A selection fills
  the input with the item's label and closes; under `multiple` it toggles,
  clears the query and stays open. A preset value's label reaches the input
  from data before any item mounts. TAGS: under `multiple` the data
  expansion renders a Tag per chosen value in the Control, before the
  Input: TagLabel + TagRemove (a real <button> in the tab order,
  aria-label "Remove <label>"; focus returns to the input), or the root's
  `tag` slot ({ value, label, item }) in their place (per-tag controls).
  Hand-written roots place <Combobox.Tags /> (scoped default slot, same
  props) in the Control themselves. A tag keeps its label after a
  consumer-filtered item unmounts. Backspace on an empty input removes the
  last value. `allowCustom`: Enter while no option is highlighted commits
  the trimmed text: a chosen value or option whose label it names
  (case-insensitive), else the text itself as the value (posted like any
  other). Under `multiple` it adds a tag and clears the input; single mode
  sets the value and closes. Typed only for string models. The popup is popover="manual" + the
  dismiss layer (native auto light dismiss would close on a caret click).
  No data-placeholder on the input — use :placeholder-shown. Home/End stay
  with the text caret; no typeahead (typing IS the filter).
  TRIGGER MODE (#58): `trigger="@"` (or a RegExp matched before the caret,
  group 1 = the query) makes the Textarea.Textarea composed INSIDE the Root
  the control — @mentions in a composer — or, single-line, an Input.Input
  (#106: /commands in a command bar; the same binding, the first control
  to claim it wins). Same scope, same Popup/Item/Group/
  Empty parts, so no new recipe; no Control/Input/Trigger/HiddenInput
  render. The token at the caret (trigger at text start or after
  whitespace, then non-whitespace) is the query (model:inputValue). Opens
  while a token exists and something matches (or emptyText is set), first
  option highlighted. While open the textarea carries role=combobox,
  aria-expanded, aria-activedescendant (aria-autocomplete=list and
  aria-controls always); ArrowUp/Down, Enter, Tab (unmodified) and Escape
  are consumed before the app's onKeydown. A commit replaces the whole token
  with trigger + label + space (reusing a following space, never two) via
  insertText (undoable), restores the caret
  after it and emits `insert` ({ value, label, text }); `model` is never
  written. `itemInsert({ item, value, key, label, prefix, query }) => string`
  (#107) replaces the default text; it is inserted verbatim (no space added
  or stepped over), caret after it; `item` is undefined for a hand-written
  option. Mousedown on the popup is prevented, so focus stays in the
  textarea. ANCHOR (#105): by default the popup docks to the textarea's
  box; `anchor={caretAnchor}` (@sigx/zero/behaviors) opens it at the token's
  first character on its own line — a hidden mirror of the textarea (font,
  padding, width, wrapping, direction) measures it, re-measured only when
  the text or width changes, following the page's and the textarea's
  scroll, clamped to the box. Opt-in by import, so a box-docked composer
  never ships it. Under rtl a top/bottom placement's alignment mirrors
  (bottom-start → bottom-end: the list's right edge at the @). A vertical
  writing-mode falls back to the box. Any `(control, index) => PositionAnchor | null`
  works.
- NumberInput: Root(model=number|null, defaultValue: number|null, min, max, step, largeStep, allowWheel,
  clampOnBlur, format, parse, name)/Label/Control/Input/IncrementTrigger/
  DecrementTrigger/HiddenInput. APG spinbutton on a real text input
  (inputmode=decimal): the input binds the DRAFT with model= (a derived
  Model: reads the display text, writes the draft); typing is an
  UNCOMMITTED draft, committed on
  blur/Enter (parse → clamp → step-snap anchored at min); stepping commits
  immediately (arrows ±step, PageUp/Down and Shift+Arrow ±largeStep —
  default 10 steps; an OFF-grid value steps to the neighbouring grid value
  in the direction of travel: 5 on step 2 → Up 6, Down 4; Home/End → min/max,
  triggers hold-to-repeat, wheel only when allowWheel AND focused).
  Control is the field chrome (ring/invalid draw there; input delegates
  focus-visible). hidden-input posts canonical String(value) — the visible
  input never carries name, so format can't corrupt form data. Empty
  commits null, never 0. Triggers are tabIndex=-1 satellites.
- RatingGroup: Root(model=number 0=none, count=5, allowHalf, deselectable,
  name/required/invalid/readonly)/Label/Control(role=radiogroup)/
  Item(index — explicit children 1..count, zero owns no iteration)/
  HiddenInput. Item's data-state is the ONE 3-value set: full|half|empty,
  driven by the DISPLAYED value (hover preview ?? committed);
  data-highlighted marks the preview range; the default slot receives
  { state, highlighted } for SVG swapping. Without a slot the item's content
  is a BARE TEXT node ★/★/☆ — half is a FULL star (the half-star codepoint
  U+2BEA is poorly covered in the common system sans stacks and renders as
  tofu), so a distinct half is the DS's job; a consumer symbol is an ELEMENT,
  which is how a DS tells them apart (:not(:has(> *)) / :has(*)).
  Keyboard moves the VALUE, not element focus (allowHalf: two per element):
  single tab stop at ceil(value), arrows ±step (0.5 with allowHalf), Home
  = smallest step, End = count, RTL flips horizontal. Pointer x decides
  halves; tap commits with the same math; pointerleave on control clears
  the preview.
- TreeView: Root(model=selected value, model:expandedValues=string[] —
  named-models convention: defaultExpandedValues + expandedValuesChange)/
  Label/Tree(role=tree)/Item(value, asChild,
  role=treeitem leaf)/Branch(value — the treeitem ELEMENT wrapping its
  group: aria-expanded+aria-level live here, it owns focus)/
  BranchTrigger(the clickable row — mirrors branch state + focus so
  recipes ring the row, never the subtree)/BranchIndicator/
  BranchContent(role=group, hidden when closed — content stays MOUNTED,
  just invisible to navigation). Keyboard walks VISIBLE nodes (the tree
  controller implements the flat list interface over them — roving and
  typeahead unchanged): Up/Down/Home/End rove, ArrowRight expands a
  closed branch then steps to first child, ArrowLeft collapses then
  climbs to the parent (RTL-mirrored), Enter/Space select — selection
  and expansion are separate acts. One tab stop: selected, else first
  visible enabled. No aria-posinset/setsize — the full tree is in the
  DOM, AT computes them. Single selection v1.
- Toggle: Root(model=pressed, defaultPressed, label, asChild) — one
  two-state <button> (aria-pressed, data-state on|off; `label` →
  aria-label for icon-only toggles). A mode you flip, not a form value
  (Switch keeps the form case). No hidden input.
- ToggleGroup: Root(model=string | string[], multiple, deselectable, loop,
  label, orientation)/Item(value, asChild). role=group of aria-pressed
  buttons (`label` names the group); the model FOLLOWS `multiple` (Select's
  rule): single mode holds the pressed value as a string ('' = none),
  `multiple` holds string[] — typed through overloads, so a string signal
  never binds a multiple group. Single mode deselects on re-click unless
  deselectable=false. Arrow keys rove focus (orientation- and RTL-aware,
  one tab stop: first enabled on item, else first enabled) WITHOUT changing
  selection; click/Space/Enter toggle. Item mirrors toggle's on|off and
  doubles it as a data-selected presence flag. Takes the form contract
  (name, form, disabled, invalid, required — adopts a Field.Root): with a
  `name` it posts through a visually-hidden <select> (hidden-input, only
  the pressed values as options) — one field in single mode, repeated
  fields under `multiple`; required blocks submit and focuses the group's
  tab stop; form reset() restores defaultValue.

Named models (first used by Combobox; the convention for every multi-state
component): a component has exactly ONE unnamed `model` — its essential
value, what `hidden-input` posts. Every additional controllable state is a
named model bound as `model:<stateName>` in JSX (sigx
`Define.Model<'<stateName>', T>`), each keeping the standard companions
`default<StateName>` + `<stateName>Change`. Combobox: `model` = selected
value, `model:inputValue` = text, `model:open` = open.

Variant axes (`color`/`size`/`variant`) are accepted by Accordion, Alert,
Avatar, Badge, Box, Breadcrumbs, Button, Drawer, Card, Chat, Checkbox, Collapsible, Combobox, Dialog,
Divider, EmptyState, Field, Indicator, Input, Join, Kbd, Menu, NumberInput,
Navbar, NavList, Pagination, Popover, Progress, RadialProgress, RadioGroup,
RatingGroup, Select, Skeleton, Slider, Spinner, Stats, Status, Steps,
Switch, Tabs, Textarea, Timeline, Toast, Toggle, ToggleGroup, Tooltip,
Table, FileUpload, Carousel, Swap, Countdown, Diff and TreeView;
that is every component. Where the Root renders a fragment (a
dialog/menu/popover/tooltip) the props live on the Trigger, which renders the
carrier part the compiled axis selectors anchor on, and Toast routes the
queue's `toast({ color })` through the same pass-through with an explicit prop
on a composed Root winning. The axes pass through as
data-* and zero attaches no styling to them. Button is the worked example:
route `color` through a component token pair (`--btn-accent` and its
content colour) that the `variant` rules read, so the two axes compose
instead of multiplying into a rule per combination.

- Recipes take conditional styles via `parts.<part>.at`, keyed by a declared
  breakpoint (emitted as `@media (min-width: ...)`), a built-in
  (`reduced-motion`, `hover-none`, `prefers-dark`, `forced-colors`) or a raw
  `@`-prefixed prelude. Nesting composes at-rules, and `at` inside `variants`
  gives responsive variants. Author mobile-first and declare breakpoints
  ascending -- declaration order is emission order. `prefers-dark` is the
  SYSTEM preference, NOT a `[data-theme]` dark theme. Stop a looping
  animation under `reduced-motion` (`animation: none`); never shorten it.
- The ramp reaches the app: `--breakpoint-<name>` on `:root`,
  `<ds>/css/breakpoints` (`@custom-media --above-<name>` / `--below-<name>`),
  and in JS `getBreakpoints()` plus `useMediaQuery({ above | below },
  { initial })` from @sigx/zero -- SSR-safe (reads `initial` until mount),
  call it in setup. `above` = `(min-width: X)`, `below` = `(width < X)`.

## Authoring a design system (@sigx/zero-kit)

defineTokens({roles?, system?, systemDark?, custom?, breakpoints?, themes,
defaultLight, defaultDark}) + defineRecipe({component, parts: {part: {base,
states, selectors}}, variants, defaultVariants}) + defineDesignSystem({name,
tokens, recipes}). `roles` declares the color vocabulary ({brand: {}, surface:
{content: false, soft: false}, …}; omitted → the recommended eight);
`system` declares the non-color token values per category ({radius: {field:
'0.5rem'}, border: '1px'}), with `systemDark` for dark-scheme overrides;
`custom` declares DS-specific tokens (name → {description, syntax?}) valued
per-theme in `custom` — all surface in the DS's dist/manifest.json, which
also lists every custom property the DS emits under `tokens.properties`.
Compile with `sigx zero:build`; check with `sigx zero:validate` (declared-role
completeness, WCAG contrast on every declared role/-content pair, state
coverage) and `sigx zero:audit` (the compiled CSS: every declared state
renders differently, indicators draw, real buttons reset `appearance`,
declared axis steps are honoured, loops stop under reduced motion; also
written as dist/audit.json by the build). Reference implementation: @sigx/zero-basic; daisyUI-flavored
skin: @sigx/zero-daisyui.

## Building your own component (ecosystem packages)

The authoring surface is public: defineAnatomy (from @sigx/zero/anatomy;
`toJSON()` emits the manifest component shape), every behavior
(@sigx/zero/behaviors: controllable state, SSR-safe ids, list/tree
registration, roving tabindex, dismissal, focus, press feedback, typeahead,
anchor positioning, createVirtualList windowing), the contract helpers (dataAttr, stateAttr, variantAttrs,
renderAsChild + synthesizesClickFrom for asChild keyboard activation), and
the conformance assertion expectAnatomy (@sigx/zero/testing — throws plain
Error, any test runner). Convention: vendor-prefix the scope (`acme-…`),
publish a manifest fragment `{package: "<npm specifier>", components:
[anatomy.toJSON()]}` and optionally a recipe pack (RecipeInput[] against the
recommended token grammar). A design system opts in by MERGING the fragment
(`mergeManifests(base, fragment)` from @sigx/zero-kit, or `--extra-manifest`
on zero:build/zero:validate) and writing or adopting a recipe; one that never
merges it leaves the component unstyled but accessible. ZeroScope stays
closed — merged scopes carry provenance and are excluded by name from the
generated register.d.ts gate. Worked example: @sigx/zero-ext-example
(in-repo), adopted by @sigx/zero-basic's build.mjs.

- https://sigx.dev/llms.txt (the framework)
- https://signalxjs.github.io/zero/manifest.json (anatomy manifest)
